bull.probability_evidence: All four regions grew in H1 2026, ROIC (32.4%), operating margin (29.7%) and FCF margin (23.1%) are near 5y highs, and P/E, EV/EBITDA and P/FCF all sit below their 5y minimums; Disney licensing titles ('Ice Age', 'Will Trent') to Netflix evidences persisting platform power (evaluation bull case; fact sheet Quality/Valuation tables; https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/disney-licenses-lineup-movies-tv-shows-netflix-including-ice-age-will-trent-2026-10-02/).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Fair value table, Bull row: DCF $35.86 vs EV/EBITDA $122.51 implies a half-spread of 46.8% of the $92.50 target (half*(122.51-35.86)/92.5); capped at the mc-inputs.json regression.residual_vol.blended ceiling of 33.5% (0.3347541375104222) per the target_band rule.

base.probability_evidence: Revenue growth is already slowing toward the ~15% H1 2026 pace shown on the income statement, without yet breaking the five-year margin/ROIC improvement trend, making a 'multiple stays compressed while growth moderates' outcome the modal case (evaluation base case basis; fact sheet income-statement regional growth figures).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Fair value table, Base row: DCF $28.84 vs EV/EBITDA $60.46 implies a half-spread of 24.4% of the $64.74 target (half*(60.46-28.84)/64.74 = 0.2442); within the mc-inputs.json regression.residual_vol.blended ceiling of 33.5%.

bear.probability_evidence: Co-CEO Sarandos said Netflix is 'not growing as fast as I want' two weeks before Q3 results (TipRanks/Bloomberg headlines, 2026-10-01); the reverse DCF requires 30.2% year-one growth versus the ~15% delivered; EV/EBITDA is still 47% above peers; and the macro overlay's moderate toward-bear tilt (real-yield-driven cost-of-equity pressure amplified by a 1.61 beta) reinforces downside (evaluation bear case; research/NFLX/2026-10-08-macro.md).

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Fair value table, Bear row: DCF -$1.39 vs EV/EBITDA $46.83 implies a half-spread of 51.5% of the $46.83 target (half*(46.83-(-1.39))/46.83); capped at the mc-inputs.json regression.residual_vol.blended ceiling of 33.5% (0.3347541375104222) per the target_band rule.

expected_12m_move.cite: mc-inputs.json factor_news.SPY headlines are mixed over 2026-10-06/07: record highs ('S&P closes at record high, breaking 7,800 points', CNBC Intl TV; 'S&P 500 Hits Record High as Big Tech Leads', Bloomberg) alongside selloff/skepticism signals on the same dates ('SPY, QQQ Pressured by Tech Selloff and Elevated Treasury Yields', TipRanks; 'Two big bearish trades point to skepticism', CNBC; 'S&P 500, Nasdaq ease from record highs as Treasury yields climb', Reuters) -- no net directional signal, set to 0 per the factor rule.

mc-inputs.json factor_news.IEF headlines skew toward a continuing bond rout as of the most recent dates ('US 30-Year Yields Return to 2002 High', Bloomberg, 2026-10-07; 'Global Bond Markets Sell Off on France's Fiscal Worries', Barrons, 2026-10-05; 'The Bond Rout Is Deepening...', WSJ, 2026-10-01), consistent with the macro overlay's facts (research/NFLX/2026-10-08-macro.md: 10y real yield DFII10 2.91% up +0.61pp over 3m, 10y nominal DGS10 5.27%, both real-rate-led); a modest negative 12m move for the Treasury-price ETF (within the +/-15% bound for non-extraordinary news).
